title: England FA weighs legal challenge to Infantino’s bid for 4th FIFA term
text:
England FA weighs legal challenge to Infantino’s bid for 4th FIFA term - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 19일(목) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports England FA weighs legal challenge to Infantino's bid for 4th FIFA term 
 입력 2026.11.19. 09:30 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Controversy is growing over FIFA President Gianni Infantino's bid for a fourth term. It has emerged that the Football Association (FA) of England even considered legally challenging Infantino's eligibility to run in the next presidential election.
 The BBC reported on the 19th, Korea time: "The Football Association considered the possibility of legal action to block Infantino's bid for a fourth term as FIFA president. However, it concluded that even if it lodged an objection, it would be unlikely to succeed."
 At the heart of the controversy is FIFA's rule limiting presidential terms.
 Infantino succeeded former FIFA President Sepp Blatter in 2016. He led efforts to introduce a rule limiting presidents to a maximum of three terms.
 In 2022, the FIFA Council decided to exclude Infantino's first term, from 2016 to 2019, when calculating his term limits.
 The reasoning was that Infantino had served the remainder of Blatter's term after Blatter stepped down before completing it, so that period should not count as a full term.
 The decision drew continued criticism. Human rights group FairSquare sent a letter to the Football Association earlier this month, arguing that FIFA's decision ran counter to the intent and purpose of its statutes and could be challenged legally.
 FairSquare said Infantino had already served the maximum of three terms and urged the FA to ask FIFA's Governance Committee to bar him from running in the presidential election next March.
 The Football Association concluded that legal action was unlikely to be effective.
 According to a letter obtained by the BBC, FA Chair Debbie Hewitt told FairSquare: "We considered challenging whether Infantino is eligible to run again for FIFA president. But we concluded that this effort would be unlikely to achieve the result we want."
 She added: "Ultimately, FIFA's internal procedures led to a decision to exclude Infantino's first term from the calculation of the maximum term limit. After carefully reviewing those procedures, we believe an objection would not succeed."
 FairSquare criticized that assessment.
 The group said: "It is understandable that the FA does not trust FIFA's internal procedures, but abandoning this route is the wrong decision. It sends Infantino the message that he can do whatever he wants."
 Miguel Maduro, a former chair of FIFA's Governance Committee, also said national football associations or continental confederations may need to challenge Infantino's eligibility through the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).
 However, Maduro also suggested that Aleksander Ceferin, president of the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), having already decided to seek a fourth term could make legal action by European football associations more difficult.
 The FA made clear that it opposes Infantino's re-election, even as it viewed the chances of legal action as low.
 Hewitt said: "We continue to oppose Infantino's re-election. We will fully support our preferred candidate, Philippe Diallo, in the next FIFA presidential election."
 Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, is challenging Infantino with UEFA's support.
 The FA had previously withdrawn its support for Infantino after his plan to sell private investors stakes in FIFA-run events, including the World Cup, sparked controversy.
 FIFA received a request from the BBC for comment on the controversy.
 FIFA had previously said that in 2022, its Council unanimously decided not to count the period from 2016 to 2019 as part of Infantino's official term.
 The FA declined to comment separately on the BBC report.
 The next FIFA presidential election is scheduled for March 2027. The debate over Infantino's bid for a fourth term is expected to continue as calls to count his first term clash with FIFA's decision to exclude it.
